content:
Here is a situation I have found myself in several times in the last few weeks.

I have a huge trace from set_option trace.profiler true, and somewhere buried deep in it is something I would like to analyse further. I stumble around opening triangles until I find an example of what I want to understand, and maybe it says something like [IsDefEq] [surprisingly large number] foo.bar.baz =?= foo.bar.baz. What must be happening here is that actually I have two terms which are not syntactically identical but which just happen to be being displayed in the same way.

Sometimes I am lucky; I can hover over the terms and spot subterms which are not identical. But sometimes I am unlucky and even the expanded terms I see on hovering look identical; the problem is deeper in the term. At this point I would like to switch pp.all on to see what's actually happening.

However if I make any edit to the file containing the declaration I'm tracing, then the entire trace collapses and I have to go back on a gigantic hunt to find the terms which I wanted to understand better. Furthermore, this hunt might be completely impossible with pp.all on because at some point I might have navigated to e.g. the 7th trace output in a given node, but now all trace outputs are 1000 lines long because terms in algebra can get quite out of hand, and it's extremely hard to count to 7.

Here are some dreams I have; I have absolutely no idea how feasible these are.

(1) Can I "pin" a node in a trace? I promise I won't change the declaration, but I might want to switch pp.all on in the file, and I want to jump straight back to the node which I was looking at (is "node" the right word? I just mean "something which starts with a [thing_like_this] and has a ▶ or ▼ at the end".

(2) Can I press a button to suddenly turn on pp.all without editing the file at all?

(3) Or can I make "hover" become "pp.all hover" somehow, when looking at a trace?

Let me remark that if I print these traces to files then they can be 400M long, they are pretty unwieldy things. Hover is super-helpful, but it's not always detailed enough. However I don't know whether (a) this is a niche use case or (b) there are serious obstructions to implementing anything like this. I can write an RFC if required but I thought I'd just ask first (I would not immediately rule out there already being a solution to this, for example!)

When I debug typeclass resolution + defeq issues, I also turn on set_option trace.Meta.isDefEq true, I find it more friendly than eyeing two terms printed with pp.all. Could this be useful for you? (it might dramatically increase your log size though)
